newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian money market rate up 60 bps to 10.1 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian money market rate up 60 bps to 10.1 pct.

text.p: Croatia's average money market rate edged up 60 basis points to 10.1 on Tuesday, boosted by the volume of term loans struck at higher rates.
Total daily settlements shrank to 13.8 million kuna, of which nine million were fresh borrowings, mostly call money struck at the steady rate of 9.0 percent.
The end of trading left a surplus of 36.2 million kuna on the supply side.
Some one-week loans were rolled over for interbank funds at 12 percent, others were struck at a higher rate of 9.6 percent, with the insurers' rate steady at 12 percent.
Overnight trade totalled 5.3 million kuna, which two banks used, one to square its position and the other to maintain its mandatory reserve.
The central bank calculated the kuna midrates for Wednesday's dealings at 5.5730 to the dollar and 3.5610 to the German mark.
